title: Product logical data model
sources: document 22, logical data model (attributes, keys, relationships, history, delete policy)
document 20, glossary and entities (names, purposes, engine contract, C40, reserved IDs)
document 21, configuration model (C40 types, column proposals)
document 24, MCP surface (C41 Tool Policy, proposal)

conventions: Names are the logical names of document 20: singular Title Case English with no prefix. A generator turns them into physical names, for example <prefix>_BusinessApplication on Dataverse and ops.BusinessApplication on Azure SQL.
required: Y required, N optional, C conditional (the rule is in the description).
ref: CFG is a configuration reference (payloads carry the row key), OPS a reference to an operational row, PR a reference to a Principal Reference (O05).
keyOf lists the configuration entities whose keys a json or key column holds. The value configuration means any configuration entity.
Every entity has Id as its primary key. keys lists business and alternate keys only.
Cardinality is written parent to child. Delete is the behavior when someone deletes the parent. Restrict is the default.
Relationship ids follow the catalog of document 22, section 6. A catalog row that covers several columns gets a letter per column. RX ids are relationships the catalog does not list.

historyClasses.name: Append-only
historyClasses.rule: Inserted once. Never updated, never deleted. C02 is inserted only by the activation operation

historyClasses.name: Freeze on final
historyClasses.rule: Editable only while in its draft state. Frozen when it reaches a final state. Never deleted after it leaves draft. O14 is final at insert. O13 has fill-once columns. C46 is frozen at submit; after that only the engine writes its outcome columns, once
historyClasses.dataverse: A synchronous plug-in refuses changes to frozen rows. Auditing on
historyClasses.azureSql: Updatable ledger table (C46, O08, O09, O10) or append-only ledger table (O14) [T16][S18]. A block predicate refuses updates to frozen rows [T13]. O13 and O22: temporal table plus engine rule

historyClasses.name: Effective-dated
historyClasses.rule: Updated in place, with history, but a fact is ended with a date, never deleted
historyClasses.entities: O03 (Retired On), O04 (Ended On), O06 (End On)

historyClasses.name: Mutable with history
historyClasses.rule: Updated in place. Every version kept

historyClasses.name: Configuration versioned
historyClasses.rule: Updated in place inside a working set, only by the activation operation. Each activation creates an immutable snapshot (C02)

deletePolicies.rule: Rows are never deleted, by anyone. The engine refuses. On Azure the database also denies it
Configuration rows. A row proposed in a draft exists only inside the draft's patch. A live row is never deleted. It retires (Is Active = No). Presets are read-only

Operational rows. A row whose meaning copy is draft can be deleted by the engine, on a person's instruction, with its owned children. After draft a row is never deleted: it is archived, withdrawn, cancelled or ended with a date

entities.name: Configuration Set Version
entities.purpose: An immutable snapshot of a set, created by the engine only at activation and stamped on operational rows. Append-only (class A in document 22)
notes: An immutable snapshot of a set, created only at activation and stamped on operational rows. Class A. No taxonomy columns. Drafts never live here. They live on C46 Configuration Draft (28, issue 3).

Document 21's earlier draft columns on C02 now split, and document 21 uses the same split: the draft states live in C46 Draft Status, while active and superseded are derived on C02 (Version Status, never stored); Base Version Number, Change Json, Validation Json and Applied Presets Json sit on both; Proposal Rationale sits on C46, reached through Source Draft.

attributes.name: Configuration Set
attributes.description: The set this snapshot belongs to

attributes.name: Version Number
attributes.description: A whole number that only goes up within the set. Assigned at activation, so discarded drafts leave no gaps

attributes.name: Version Status
attributes.description: Derived, never stored: active when C01 Current Version points here, superseded when a later version exists. So the append-only row is never updated. The draft and discarded states live on C46

attributes.name: Base Version Number
attributes.description: The active version this one replaced. Empty on version 1

attributes.name: Source Draft
attributes.description: The accepted draft this version came from. Required for every version after version 1

attributes.name: Change Json
attributes.description: The patch actually applied: the ordered upsert and retire operations by entity and key, after any rebase (document 21, section 4.5). Required for every version after version 1

attributes.name: Content Json
attributes.description: The full snapshot of every row in the set

attributes.name: Content Hash
attributes.description: SHA-256 of the canonical snapshot, so a record can prove which rules applied

attributes.name: Snapshot Schema Version
attributes.description: The version of the snapshot's own shape. The engine refuses a major version it does not know (document 25)

attributes.name: Validation Json
attributes.description: The validation result at activation: no errors, and any warnings with rule IDs (document 21, V01 to V44)

attributes.name: Applied Presets Json
attributes.description: The full preset and overlays applied, each with its content version. Required on version 1 and on any version that re-bases on a preset or applies an upgrade

attributes.name: Published On
attributes.description: When this version came into force, at activation

attributes.name: Instructed By
attributes.description: The admin, a person, who decided the change (D-10)

attributes.name: Change Decision
attributes.description: The configuration change or gate policy change decision behind this version. Required for every version after version 1

attributes.name: Change Summary
attributes.description: A plain list of what changed from the previous version, computed by the engine from the diff. Never the AI's own text

attributes.name: Seed Version
attributes.description: The product release whose seed this version started from, if any

relationships.note: Both set by the activation operation

entities.name: Preset
entities.purpose: A shipped, read-only configuration set a client applies, copies and adjusts. Stored as a Configuration Set whose kind is preset. A full preset or an overlay
notes: Stored as a C01 row whose Set Kind is preset, using its Preset Key and Product Release columns. Read-only: only a product upgrade writes it.

Document 21, section 3.3 proposes manifest fields for presets (Extends, Conflicts With, Areas, Content Version, Schema Version, Setup Notes Json, Checked On). They live in the preset bundle and its C02 snapshot, not in columns, so the model does not list them.
